key_insight: Eigenvalue-based neural constitutive models jointly learn flexible yield functions and evolution laws while enforcing isotropy, convexity, and thermodynamic consistency by construction.
engineering_relevance: The approach enables learned rate-independent elastoplastic material behavior, including non-associative flow, to be used in finite element boundary-value simulations.
method: Use permutation-invariant spectral representations to enforce isotropy and convexity.
Construct non-associative yield functions by adding a jointly learned term to a convex flow potential.
Train through a backward-Euler return map using implicit gradients and eigenvalue-degeneracy-aware differentiation.
evidence_signal: Evaluation includes reproducing known constitutive models, learning from full-field finite element stress–strain data and homogenized foam responses, and solving plane-stress boundary-value problems.
watch_item: Implementation requires careful implicit-solver differentiation near repeated eigenvalues; the stated scope is rate-independent, isotropic elastoplasticity.
paper_title: Thermodynamically consistent neural constitutive models for elastoplasticity via eigen-representations
